 Judgment

Wife and mother of deceased Srikantha Muganura filed petition under Section 166 of IMV Act claiming compensation worth of Rs.28,00,000/- from the respondents, who are the insurer and owner of Tractor and Trailer bearing No.KA-41-T-1442 and KA-41-T-1443 alleging that on 23.05.2017 at 7.45 p.m. near Hulikal bus stop , Magadi taluk, driver of Tractor and Trailer bearing No.KA-41-T-1442 and KA-41-T-1443 negligently without putting brakes properly and leaving key in the key point , left the Tractor and Trailer , at that point of time, Srikantha Muganura by misconception touched the key, therefore, the Tractor and Trailer started to move Srikantha Muganura fell under the wheel , suffered grievous injuries , then on the way to the hospital succumbed to those injuries.
2. As on the date of accident , Srikantha Muganura being aged about 35 years, used to earn Rs.16,000/p.m. by working as Manager in Agriculture farm of Vittal Gonabala, and used to contribute entire income to the family.
3. Regarding accident Kudur police registered crime No.185/2017.
4. In response to the notice, respondent No.1, insurance company appeared through his Advocate filed written statement denying the reason and mode of accident, age, occupation , income of the deceased, subsistence of the policy.
Respondent No.1 specifically stated that due to the negligence of Srikantha Muganura the accident taken place.
5. Inspite of the service of notice, the respondent No.2 owner of the Tractor and Trailer remained absent.

6. On the basis of the pleadings on 29.06.2019, this Authority has framed the following issues:
1. Whether the petitioners prove that the deceased succumbed to injuries in a Motor Vehicle Accident that occurred on 23.05.2017 at about 7.45 p.m. near Bus stand, Hulikal, Kudur hobli, Magadi Taluk, within the jurisdiction of Kudur police station, on account of rash and negligent driving of the Tractor and Trailer bearing No.KA-41-T-1442 and KA-41-T-1443 by its driver?
2. Whether the petitioners are entitled for compensation ?
If so, how much and from whom?

7. On 19.07.2019, 09.09.2019 , 18.09.2021 petitioner No.1 Roopa deposed as PW1 and produced 13 documents at Ex.P.1 to P.13.

On 15.12.2021, 16.02.2022, 25.03.2022, 28.06.2023, 02.08.2024 petitioners produced the evidence of T.N.Gonabala, Ramanna Gonabala , Smt.Vidya Vittal @
Vidyavathi Vital Gonabala, Tippeswamy, Senior Motor Vehicle Inspector, RTO office, Electronic City, K.P.Sathyanarayan as PW2 to 6 and get produced 2 documents at Ex.P.14 and P.14(a) to (i).

On 01.03.2024, 04.04.2024, 03.07.2024, 08.07.2024, respondent No.1 produced the evidence of officer of the insurance company as RW1 and produced authority letter at Ex.R.1.
8.
I heard the arguments submitted on behalf of both the contesting parties and perused the records.

9. On the basis of material on record, my findings on the above issues are as under:
Issue No.1 ... Due to the negligence of Srikantha Muganura , accident taken place resulting in the death of Srikantha Muganura Issue No.2 ...

Compensation is assessed at Rs.24,14,000/- with current and future interest at 6%p..a.
Issue No.3 ...

As per final order for the following:-
REASONS 10. Issues No.1 and 2 :- In the lengthy argument , learned Advocate appearing for the petitioner by analysing the evidence available in the file, submitted that negligence of the driver of Tractor and Trailer bearing No.KA-41-T- 1442 and KA-41-T-1443 is the reason for the accident by relying on the following judgments:
1. 1987 AIR 1184 ( Skanda Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Kokilaben Chandravadan and others) D.D. 01.04.1987 11.

sentences.text: In the lengthy argument learned advocate appearing for the insurance company by analysing the evidence available in the file, submitted that negligence of Srikantha Muganura was the sole reason for the incident.
12. In the light of the submission made on behalf of both the parties and with reference to the judgments cited above , I have appreciated the materials available in the file.

13. In the evidence affidavit PW1 stated that on 23.05.2017 at 7.45 p.m. near Hulikal bus stop ,
Magadi taluk, driver of Tractor and Trailer bearing No.KA-41-T- 1442 and KA-41-T-1443 negligently without putting brakes properly by leaving key in the key point , left the Tractor and Trailer , at that point of time Srikantha Muganura by misconception touched the key, therefore, the Tractor and Trailer started to move Srikantha Muganura fell under the wheels, thereby suffered grievous injuries , then on the way to the hospital succumbed to those injuries.

sentences.text: In the written statement respondent No.1 insurance company asserted that due to the sole negligence of Srikantha Muganura the incident/ accident taken place.
15. In the cross-examination PW1 stated that Srikantha, her husband studied upto SSLC had no driving licence .

PW1 stated that the driver of the Tractor and Trailer left the key in the tractor itself and stopped the tractor in a slope area and her husband went near the tractor and touched the tractor , then tractor started moving , her husband fell down, thereby accident occurred.
16. PW1 denied the suggestion that her husband without the knowledge of driving started the parked Tractor.

17. In the evidence affidavit PW2 T.N.Gonabala , S/o. Late Namadevappa , PW3 Ramanna Gonabala, S.o. Pundaleekappa cousins of petitioner No.2 Maganur Rukmini, hear say witnesses of the incident reiterated the same facts as asserted by the petitioners in the petition and in the evidence affidavits about the reason and mode of accident.
18. In the cross-examination PW2 and 3 submitted that the deceased had no driving licence and denied the suggestion that due to the negligence act on the part of the deceased accident taken place.

19. In the evidence affidavit PW4 respondent No.2 Vidya Vittal @ Vidyavathi Vittal Gonabala , an hear say witness of the incident reiterated the same facts as narrated by the petitioners in the petition and in the evidence affidavit by PW1 about the incident, occupation and income of Srikantha Muganura .

20. In the evidence PW5 B.Tippeswamy , Senior Motor Vehicle Inspector , RTO office , Electronic City, stated the rules and regulations to stop or park any vehicle by applying the brake in first gear and keep signal in the front and rear part of the so parked vehicles.

21. In the evidence PW5 after reading Ex.P.11 chargesheet stated that the driver of the Tractor and Trailer would not have left the key in the key hole in that regard firstly driver is at fault, secondly the person who has started the Tractor and Trailer by using the key of the vehicle which is left in the key hole is also at fault.

22. In the cross-examination made on behalf of the insurance company PW5 submitted inability to say that the accident was occurred due to the fault of the deceased who has started Tractor and Trailer which has been parked by the driver leaving the key in the key hole and the deceased was having knowledge that the driver has left the key in the vehicle.
PW5 submitted ignorance to the suggestion that contents of the chargesheet are correct.

23. In the evidence PW6 who worked as Police Inspector during 2017-18 at Bydarahalli police station, stated that he never conducted investigation pertaining to crime No.185/2017 of Kudur police station, however, while filing Nandish, Circle Police Inspector , Magadi circle typed his name as Investigation Officer, made signature on the typed name.

sentences.text: In the evidence affidavit RW1, Officer of insurance company , hear say witness has reiterated the same facts as narrated in the written statement .
25. It is undisputed fact that the evidence of the hear say witness are neither relevant nor believable to decide the dispute by any Court of law.

26. Ex.P.1 is the copy of the FIR and complaint, pertaining to crime No.185/2017 registered by Kudur police on 24.05.2017 against Tractor and Trailer driver Srikantha i.e., driver of Tractor and Trailer bearing No.KA- 41-T-1442 and KA-41-T-1443 for having committed offence punishable under Section 279,304(A) of IPC regarding the accident taken place at 7.45 p.m. on 23.05.2017 resulting in the death of Srikantha Muganura on the basis of complaint presented by Vittal Gonabala, S/o. Namadevappa, husband of the respondent No.2.
27.
Ex.P.2 is the copy of the P.M.Report.
Ex . P.3

is the copy of Inquest mahazar report, Ex.P.4 is the copy of spot mahazar recorded on 24.05.2017, Ex.P.5 is the copy of the sketch of the place of accident, Ex.P.6 is the copy of the notice dated 30.05.2017 issued by Investigation Officer to the respondent No.2 under Section 133 of IMV Act.

Ex.P.7 is the reply dated 13.06.2017 submitted by respondent No.2 to the Investigation Officer to the notice issued under Section 133 of IMV Act stating that as on the date of incident Tractor and Trailer had insurance coverage and submitted ignorance whether Srikantha had licence to drove Tractor and Trailer or not.
28. Ex.P.8 is the copy of Property Report No.90/2017, Ex.P.9 is the copy of the indemnity bond dated 13.06.2017 executed by respondent No.2 before Investigation Officer .

Ex.P.10 is the Motor Vehicle Accident Report , Ex.P.11 is the copy of (abated) chargesheet filed by Kudur police station in crime No.185/2017 against Srikantha Muganura , S/o. Aiyappa , driver of Tractor and Trailer bearing No.KA-41-T-1442 and KA-41-T-1443 for having committed offence punishable under Section 279,304(A) of IPC .

29 . In this case there are no reasons to disbelieve the contents of police records regarding reason ,
mode and consequence of the accident.
As referred above, in this case the evidence of the eye witness of the incident are not available.

Hence, I have concluded that on 23.05.2017 at 7.45 p.m.
near Hulikal bus stop , Magadi taluk, when driver of Tractor and Trailer bearing No.KA-41-T-1442 and KA-41-T-1443 parked the Tractor and Trailer by leaving the key in the key point , Srikantha Muganura without licence negligently touched the key or started the Tractor and Trailer by using the key, made Tractor and Trailer to move , made wheels of the Tractor and Trailer to run over him ,
thereby became the reason for the accident, resulting in his death.

Hence, I answer issue No.1 accordingly (due to the sole negligence of Srikantha Muganura accident taken place resulting in his death).
30. Issue No.2:

In the evidence PW1 stated that as on the date of accident Srikantha Muganura being aged about 35 years, used to earn Rs.16,000/p.m. by managing agricultural operations of the agricultural Firm of Vittal Gonabala and used to contribute entire income to the family.

sentences.text: In the evidence affidavit PW2 to 4 cousin brothers of petitioners No.2 and owner of the Tractor and Trailer reiterated the same facts as asserted by PW1 regarding occupation and income of deceased.

In the evidence PW4 produced 9 receipts at Ex.P.14(a) to (i) signed by Srikantha Muganura confirming receipt of Rs.16,000/p.m.
32.
In the cross-examination PW4 stated that 4 labourers are working under her and non taking of any policy under Workman Compensation Act .
PW4 submitted that receipt marked at P.14 are maintained by the deceased himself which are available with his wife, those are collected from his wife (petitioner No.1).
33. In the evidence PW5 , Senior Motor Vehicle Inspector, R.T.O. office, Electronic City, Bengaluru and PW6 Circle Inspector stated nothing regarding occupation and income of the deceased.
34. In the evidence affidavit , RW1 Officer of insurance company stated nothing regarding occupation and income of the deceased.
35. In the police records, age of the deceased is noted as 35 years.
36. Aadhar card shows that petitioner No.1 and 2 are the wife and mother of the deceased.
37. In this case documents regarding age of the deceased, aadhar card , credentials are not produced.

In the 9 receipts marked at Ex.P.14(a) to (I) it is noted that on 06.09.2016, 06.10.2016,
06.11.2016, 06.12.2016, 06.01.2017, 06.02.2017, 06.03.2017, 06.04.2017, 06.05.2017 received Rs.16,000/- each from respondent No.2 for the work of Supervisor.
38.
In this case , at this stage, there are no reasons to disbelieve the evidence of stated by petitioners regarding age, occupation and income of the deceased Srikantha Muganura .

Hence, I have calculated loss of dependency in the following terms:
Age of the deceased as on the date of 35 years accident Income of the deceased as on the date of - Rs.16,000/- accident Add : 50% towards future prospects Rs.24,000/-
(16,000 x 50% = 8,000) =16,000/-=8,000/- =Rs.24,000/-
Less : 1/3rd towards personal expenses of Rs.16,000/- the deceased (24,000 - 8,000/- = 16,000)
Annual income of the deceased Rs.1,92,000 Loss of dependency 192000x16 Rs.30,72,000 39.

Hence, loss of dependency is assessed at Rs. 30,72,000/-, Rs.15,000/- towards loss of estate and Rs.15,000/- towards funeral expenses and Rs.40,000/- towards spousal consortium to petitioner No.1, Rs.40,000/- towards loss of filial consortium to petitioner No.2.
40.
Therefore, the total compensation assessed is Rs.31,82,000/- with current and future interest at 6% p.a.

Roopa Muganura vs Tata Aig Gen Ins Co Ltd on 8 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/14669638/
6 41.

entities.text: Roopa Muganura vs Tata Aig Gen Ins Co Ltd on 8 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In this case respondent No.1 insurance company admitted the subsistence of the policy with respect to Tractor and Trailer bearing No.KA-41-T-1442 and KA-41-T- 1443 .
In the file there are no documents to show as on the date of accident Srikantha Muganura had licence to drive Tractor and Trailer .
Srikantha Muganura without licence started the Tractor and Trailer , thereby became the reason for the incident resulting in his death.
42. In view of the finding recorded on issue No.1 , petitioners are not entitle to receive the compensation from the respondents.

Hence, I answer issue No.2 accordingly and pass the following :
ORDER
The petition filed under Section 166 of IMV Act by wife and mother of Srikantha Muganura claiming compensation from the respondents is hereby dismissed.
There is no order as to costs.
